title: THE SECOND WAVE
logline: A single light learns to run and becomes a swell that floods a city of desks in about 5 months. When the water drains back, it turns out it only reached 16% of the work, and throwing more agents at the problem multiplies the errors. Then the ridge on the horizon starts to move. It is not a mountain range. It is the next wave, a structured software factory, and Opus 5.5 is the light at its crest.
spine: Oct 2025: agents 'just don't work' (a lone spark sputters on a black sea)
BUT Opus 4.5 ships in Nov 2025, and the spark ignites and runs
THEREFORE it becomes a swell that passes 5 accelerating gates, and run-rate rolls from ~$9B to $30B+ (Anthropic-reported)
THEREFORE about 5 months from capability to budget. The wave breaks over the city of desks (75% of new code at Google is AI-generated)
BUT the water drains back: writing code is 16% of dev time, and Review, Test and Deploy are still dark. What about the other 84%?
THEREFORE the obvious fix: more agents rain onto the city
BUT with independent agents, errors multiply ×17.2. The swarm collapses and the sea draws back, as it does before a tsunami
BUT the ridge on the horizon is moving. That's not the horizon: it's the next wave, the software factory

THEREFORE structure instead of a crowd: a graph for control, a hierarchy for coherence, swarms only for parallel work. With a coordinator, errors fall to ×4.4, and ~30,000 agents already run at once inside Anthropic
BUT a factory needs someone to run the floor: who runs the factory?
THEREFORE Opus 5.5: 100-agent teams pick their own structure, one session directs a dozen, 18+ hours unattended, Fable 5.1-level work at 40% lower cost vs Opus 5
THEREFORE the second wave breaks over the whole line. The cold open plays again, now warm
BUT the clock is running: if the pattern holds, budgets follow in early 2027 (labelled as a projection)
motifs: THE SPARK (protagonist light; clay orb r0.1, emissive 12-14, 16-point ribbon trail): it sputters alone (Act I) → ignites and runs (Opus 4.5) → surfs the crest → gets knocked off-line in the flat swarm → sits alone on the drained sea floor and turns toward the horizon → sits at the apex of the factory wave's hierarchy (Opus 5.5) → ends alone again in the frame-0 composition while the horizon ignites behind it (button). It appears in 20+ shots and changes state 6 times.

THE HORIZON LINE → THE WAVE: a 1px HDR line (shot 10). A dark ridge is planted 3 times (shots 8, 11, 31), compressed by a 200mm lens so it reads as a mountain range, and it stands taller than the first wave yet never moves. Shots 58-60 reveal it as the factory wave, 50× bigger (the 'those aren't mountains' turn). The same line becomes the light-line forge that opens the title, and it ignites end to end in the button.

THE DESK LAMPS (the city of desks; 1,200-1,600 instanced glowBoxes): steel-blue lamps mean human speed, clay lamps mean an agent is working. The first wave flips them to clay (Act I). When the water drains, only 16% stay lit, and that lit cluster forms the '16%' card. The mirror tour re-shoots the dark Review/Test/Deploy compositions, now lit and flowing. The button ends on a top-down cascade of every lamp lighting L→R.

SOUND MOTIF: the tick (clock spine) on every beat in Act I, alone in the tick-only passage, and back alone in the button; plus a 5-note figure D-F-A-G-F that is sparse on the pulse in Act I, full in the climax, and becomes the add9 shimmer under the title.
music_plan:
KEY D minor. Master grid 120 BPM (beat 0.5 s / 15 f, bar 2.0 s) for 0:00-1:32; tempo lift to 150 BPM (beat 0.4 s / 12 f, bar 1.6 s) for 1:32.0-1:59.2; the 120 BPM tick returns for the title and button (2:00-2:15). One cue list drives audio and picture, and cuts land 0-1 f before transients.
COLD OPEN 0:00-0:08 (intensity 8): f0 impact + sub_drop + tick + 2 f bloom flash; noise riser 0.5→2.0; reverse_swell ends 2.0; BRAAM #1 (D1, 4 s tail) + impact at 0:02.0; hit A 4.0 with a D6 ping; tom 5.5; tape_stop over 1 octave 6.0-6.7; single tick at 7.5 over the drone floor (not silence).
ACT I 0:08-0:40 (−22 → −15 LUFS-S): D-A drone + tick on quarters + D6 pings on cards (0:08-0:16). MOOD CHANGE #1 at 0:16.0: pulse ostinato on 8ths ('x..x..x.x..x..x.'); i-bVI-bVII-i (Dm Bb/D C/D Dm), 2 bars per chord. Risset ticks accelerate under the 5 gates (0:18-0:28). Whooshes peak on the gate passes at 18.5 / 21.5 / 26.25 / 27.25. Pulse moves to 16ths at 0:24. Counter click + hit at 25.0; hit + sub at 28.0. string_swell from 30.0; 2-bar noise riser 36.0→38.0 with a suckback ending exactly at 38.0; impact + string peak at 38.0 (wave break).
ACT II 0:40-1:04 (−17 → −13, then a −26 dip): pulse low-passed, Shepard bed at 0.08 oct/s, −28 dB. Tricolon hits 44.0 tom / 45.0 tom+metal / 45.5 tom+metal+sub. Glitch bursts on the swarm (49.0, 50.0, 53.0, 54.0; 4 of the 6 allowed). Suckback 55.0→56.0. MUSIC STOP on the 0:56 downbeat: tick + drone only for 56-63.5 (the clock spine left naked). reverse_swell (organ-like Dm string) 62.0→63.5. SILENCE DROP #1 63.5-64.0 (15 f, all buses gated to zero including tails).
ACT III-A 1:04-1:32 (−13 → −10): BRAAM #2 (D1) + impact + sub_drop on 1:04.0 on the reveal-completion frame. MOOD CHANGE #2 at 1:06.0: full hybrid percussion (16th pulse '3+3+2', hits on beats 1 and 3, Dm Bb F C), data_chirps under the fleet shots. Structure tricolon 72.0 / 74.0 / 76.0 with layers added each time (tom → +metal → +sub). Shepard riser at 0.33 oct/s plus noise riser 84.0→89.0, hard cut at 89.0. SILENCE DROP #2 89.0-90.0 (30 f digital zero). 90.0 single tick under the typed line; sub thumps at 90.5 and 91.0; 0.75 s suckback ends at 92.0.
ACT III-B 1:32-1:59.2 at 150 BPM (−10 → −8): MOOD CHANGE #3 on 92.0, the climax theme with a Bb→D-major lift (the solution chord), widest stereo, choir/brass pads, and the 16th ostinato at 3 f. Impact + sub_drop + clay flash on 92.0 (no braam). Proof cards each get a click + hit, varied ±2 st with alternating metal 310/370 Hz. Mirror tour runs a hip-hop micro-montage with one SFX per shot (clunk, servo, stamp, chime). Theme peaks at 112.8 (bookend). Final tricolon 114.4 / 115.2 / 116.0 with escalating layers. Hit run: quarter hits 116.8-117.6, then 8ths, then a glitch roll 1/16→1/64, noise riser + snare roll, and a tape-stop on the last 8th. Suckback ends 119.2. SILENCE DROP #3 (false stop) 119.2-120.0 (24 f).
TITLE 2:00.0: BRAAM #3 = final sting (D1+A1 power chord, no third) + biggest impact (0 dB) + sub_drop + logo_shimmer (D add9 bell, RT60 7 s). Exposure +1.5 EV decaying over 20 f. The music does not resolve.
BUTTON 2:04-2:12: the tick returns alone at −26 dB at 120 BPM; data_chirps under the horizon ignition; 1-bar riser 129.0→130.0; final hit + micro-sting (chirp burst + −12 dB impact + ping) at 130.0; 1.5 s ring-out.
END 2:12-2:15: pad and shimmer tail decaying below −60 dBFS by f4049; the only fade is the last 15 f.
Totals: 3 braams (0:02, 1:04, 2:00), 3 silence drops, 3 mood changes, 9 flashes, 4 tier-S hits. Master at −14 LUFS-I and ≤ −1 dBTP.

acts.name: COLD OPEN: Flash-forward
acts.purpose: Frame-0 spectacle: the spark, the lamp cascade and a fogged glimpse of the colossal wave. '≈5 MONTHS.' / 'THE FIRST WAVE.' opens L1 (what is the second?), then a rewind.
acts.grade: Warm preview: clay on void, sat 1.0

acts.name: ACT I: The First Wave
acts.purpose: From 'they just don't work' to a budget line. The spark ignites (Opus 4.5), swells through 5 accelerating gates, the run-rate rolls, '≈5 MONTHS: CAPABILITY → BUDGET', and the wave breaks over the city of desks. The ridge is planted as 'mountains'.
acts.grade: Cool slate/steel, sat 0.9; clay only on the spark and the lamps it lights

acts.name: ACT II: The Undertow
acts.purpose: Problem statement. The water drains back: 16% of dev time is code, and Review/Test/Deploy stay dark (L2: the other 84%?). 'More agents' fails at ×17.2 errors. The sea draws back like a tsunami precursor, then 'that's not the horizon.'
acts.grade: Cold steel/ice, sat 0.8, red alert pinpoints only; handheld 0.3°, Dutch ±8-12°

acts.name: ACT III-A: The Second Wave
acts.purpose: The Interstellar turn: the ridge is a wave 50× bigger, and it is structure. 'IT'S THE NEXT WAVE.' / 'SOFTWARE FACTORY.' Graph / hierarchy / swarm; errors ×17.2 → ×4.4 with a coordinator; ~30,000 agents at once inside Anthropic. Ends on black: 'who runs the factory?' (L3).
acts.grade: Warming: ivory and clay structure on void, sat 1.0; machine grammar (no handheld, level horizon, symmetry)

acts.name: ACT III-B: Who Runs the Factory
acts.purpose: Reveal: the light at the apex is OPUS 5.5. Verified proof volley (system card, Stripe, Clio, cost), a mirror tour of the once-dark stations, the warm cold-open bookend, the PEAK at 112.8-116.8 (83.6-86.5%), the final tricolon and recall flurry, then the false stop.
acts.grade: Warm: clay 10-20% of frame, brass/ivory, sat 1.05

acts.name: TITLE
acts.purpose: Light-line forge: CLAUDE OPUS 5.5 on BRAAM #3. 4 s hold, nothing else on screen.

acts.name: BUTTON
acts.purpose: Callback plus hook. The frame-0 composition returns calm; 'if the pattern holds:' / 'BUDGETS IN EARLY 2027.' (PROJECTION) as the whole horizon ignites; final hit. L4 left open: the clock is running.

acts.name: END CARD
acts.purpose: Lockup and a true credit wink: the film was made with Opus 5.5 agents.

why_it_works: The film is one physical metaphor that runs from start to finish, so it never reads like a slideshow. The first wave is a light that swells, floods a city and drains back, and the viewer feels both the speed (5 gates at 3.5 → 0.5 s intervals) and the limit (only 16% of the lamps stay lit). The Interstellar re-read is planted three times: the ridge is compressed by a 200mm lens into what looks like a mountain range, it stands taller than the first wave, and it never moves. The tsunami draw-back makes the turn feel physically inevitable, and the letterbox opens on the same braam. Angles carry meaning: worm's-eye for threat and awe, top-down for 'see the system' (the 16% map, the formation snap), telephoto for compression and the misread, macro for the protagonist. The two Act-II shots that state the problem come back as mirror shots that answer it: the ×17.2 cloud snaps to ×4.4, and the dark Review/Test/Deploy stations come back lit. Energy rises as a sawtooth: Act I ASL is about 1.14 s; Act III-B is 0.72 s at a 150 BPM lift with 6 f recalls; there are 3 braams, 3 silences, a peak at 84-86% of runtime, then a false stop, a 4 s title and a button that leaves the clock running. Every on-screen claim traces to facts.md, keeps its source tag, and stays within the 138-word budget.
risks: Word budget is tight: 138 on-screen words, counting the 2-3 word source tags. Any added card or tag breaks the ≤140 limit. Cut a tag's date before cutting a card.

Derived and framing lines are not literal facts.md claims: 'THE OTHER 84%?' is 100−16 posed as a question; 'IT'S THE NEXT WAVE.', 'SOFTWARE FACTORY.', 'GRAPH: CONTROL.' etc. and 'THE WHOLE LINE.' are thesis framing with no numbers. They need legal/brand sign-off, or swap 'THE WHOLE LINE.' for a station-only image.

Attribution traps: '~30,000 AGENTS AT ONCE' is Anthropic-internal (Aug 2026), before Opus 5.5, so it must stay in Act III-A and never be framed as an Opus 5.5 result. '40% LOWER COST' must keep 'VS OPUS 5'. Never imply Opus 5.5 is the most capable model (Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 sit above it).
The same hero spark plays Opus 4.5 (first wave) and Opus 5.5 (apex). Viewers may read this as one model; the 'OPUS 4.5 — NOV 2025' card and the warm-grade change must make the evolution clear.
Shot 49 (lock-gate jam) and shot 92 (40 slabs) illustrate Cursor and Stripe facts without cards. Keep them clearly metaphorical, and drop shot 49 if anyone could read it as a claim.

The Interstellar turn only works if the ridge is planted and readable at phone size. Test shots 8, 11 and 31 muted at 25% scale. If the ridge reads as noise, raise its rim highlight and lower the fog to 70%.
Render budget: the ocean (30k points), the wave lattice and the log zoom (shot 72) sit at the per-shot particle cap. Use fog instead of DOF, and budget about 1.6 h for 135 s at 0.7 s/frame.

Tempo map changes 120 → 150 → 120 BPM, but engine beats() reads a global BPM. Write Act III-B durations as literal seconds (multiples of 0.4) and give the audio renderer an explicit tempo segment from 92.0 to 119.2.
Flash and photosensitivity: 9 flashes in total. The 6 f recall flurry (117.6-119.2) must stay luminance-matched within ±8%, with no white flashes inside it.
Act III-B ASL (0.72 s) is just above the bible's 0.6× Act I target (0.68 s). If the cut feels plateaued, split shots 103/104 into four 0.4 s cuts.
The Interstellar line must not be quoted verbatim, and no film assets may be used; 'that's not the horizon.' is the homage.
